READING

**The financial arithmetic first**

The rent gap is £214,000 − £118,000 = £96,000 a year. Against that, Culverstone carries a dead-mileage penalty. The 44/44A network runs 22 vehicles to the Verrancombe Bridge stand, 313 days a year, over a distance that is 3 miles further than from Hallowbrand. Round-trip per vehicle per day: 6 extra miles. Annual extra cost: 22 × 6 × 313 × £0.63 = £26,029, call it £26,000. Net annual saving under KESTERWICK once running: £96,000 − £26,000 = £70,000.

Over the ten-year term that is £700,000. The capital call is £40,000 deposit plus £480,000 of works = £520,000. Simple payback is 7.4 years inside the term, leaving roughly 2.6 years of clear benefit. Net 10-year advantage to KESTERWICK, before any transition costs: approximately £180,000.

**Transition risk under worst-case planning**

The application was validated 2026-08-14. Thirteen weeks out is 2026-11-13—before both the Faskally deposit deadline (2026-12-05) and the Hallowbrand deadline (2026-12-19). There is therefore a slim but real chance planning clears before the option has to be locked. That is a bonus, not a plan. The decision must be made on harder ground.

At 34 weeks (the median): consent around 2027-04-09, plus 22 weeks construction puts occupation around 2027-09-11. That is more than two months before the Hallowbrand lease expires on 2027-11-30. No gap, no Nethercote, no workshop interruption.

At 61 weeks (the county's recorded ceiling): consent around 2027-10-28, occupation around 2028-03-25. Hallowbrand ends 2027-11-30. The gap is approximately four months. At £18,500 a month that is £74,000 and, critically, no workshop: maintenance would need to be contracted out. Call the outsourced workshop cost conservatively £30,000–£50,000 for four months on 31 vehicles.

Worst-case transition penalty: roughly £120,000–£125,000 in total, which cuts the 10-year net advantage from £180,000 to perhaps £55,000–£80,000. KESTERWICK is still ahead on the numbers even at the tail of the distribution.

**The option deposit holds past the worst case**

This is the structural point that makes KESTERWICK viable even under Verrancombe's slowest recorded determination. The £40,000 deposit secures Culverstone to 2028-06-30. The worst-case occupation date (61 weeks + 22 weeks = 2028-03-25) falls comfortably inside that window. There is no scenario within the recorded distribution under which the site lapses before the building is complete. The mechanism Faskally has offered is correctly sized for the risk.

**The 44/44A bid deadline**

Bids are due 2027-09-14 and depot cost is a fixed line. This is the single most consequential variable in the decision and it cuts strongly in favour of KESTERWICK.

Under ARDENSHAW the bid carries £214,000/year. Under KESTERWICK:

— Median case: Culverstone is operational by September 2027. The bid carries £118,000 + £26,000 = £144,000/year.
— Worst case: At the bid date Culverstone is not yet consented. However, the deposit holds the site to 2028-06-30, construction on the worst determination finishes 2028-03-25, and the new contract term starts 2028-04-01. The numbers fit. Trentmoor can bid Culverstone's cost with full confidence that the depot will be operational at contract commencement.

The competitive bid value of a £70,000/year lower depot cost line is not a nice-to-have. The 44/44A network is 22 of Trentmoor's 31 vehicles. Losing the contract, or being squeezed on margin to retain it, would outweigh every other consideration in this analysis. KESTERWICK is the only course that keeps the depot cost competitive in 2027.

**Cash**

£640,000 cash and £200,000 undrawn. The capital call is £520,000, spread over time: the £40,000 deposit in December 2026, then the £480,000 over 22 weeks of construction (which begins after consent, at earliest late 2026, more likely mid-2027). The company will be generating operating cash throughout. The facility is not touched by the deposit alone. The timing of draw-down is manageable and the liquidity does not constrain the choice.

**What ARDENSHAW actually costs**

ARDENSHAW is not the safe option; it is the expensive certain option. It commits £214,000/year for ten years—£2,140,000 total—against KESTERWICK's £1,180,000 rent plus £260,000 dead mileage plus £520,000 capital plus up to £125,000 worst-case transition = approximately £2,085,000 even in the tail scenario. The landlord's offer at Hallowbrand represents a 52% rent increase for no new capability. Trentmoor would leave 2037 still a tenant, with no accumulated equity in the site and no competitive cost base.

**Summary**

The numbers favour KESTERWICK across every scenario within the recorded planning distribution. The Faskally deposit is correctly sized to cover the slowest determination the county has produced. The 44/44A bid—the most operationally critical event in the forecast period—is more winnable from Culverstone. The four-month worst-case Nethercote exposure is the main genuine risk, and it is bounded, quantifiable and still leaves KESTERWICK ahead. ARDENSHAW offers certainty at a ten-year cost that cannot be justified.

---

READING
The rent differential net of dead mileage yields £70,000/year in favour of KESTERWICK; the £520,000 capital cost pays back within the lease term; the Faskally deposit mechanism covers even Verrancombe's slowest-ever 61-week determination, with Culverstone coming available just before the new 44/44A contract commences in April 2028; and the £70,000/year lower depot cost line in the September 2027 bid is the most consequential single number in the decision, because the 44/44A network is 22 of 31 vehicles and losing it on price would exceed any other cost in this analysis.

CALL
KESTERWICK

GROUNDS
The Faskally deposit holds Culverstone through even Verrancombe's recorded worst-case determination and subsequent construction, the ten-year net saving over Hallowbrand renewal remains positive in every scenario including a full Nethercote gap, and the £70,000-a-year lower depot cost in the September 2027 contract bid is the figure that most directly governs the company's revenue base.
